text.p: Grand Casinos Inc chairman and chief executive officer Lyle Berman said he expects 1997 earnings per share in the $1.40 to $1.60 range.
"We are comfortable in that range of $1.50, plus or minus a dime," Berman told Reuters following the casino and hotel operator's shareholder meeting here on Friday.

In 1996, Grand Casinos had $1.16 in earnings per share, excluding a $3.59 per share write-off of its equity participation in Stratosphere Corp including both Grand Casinos' investments and its share of operating losses.
Stratosphere opened a casino-hotel complex in Las Vegas in April last year, and filed for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in January of this year.
Berman assured the shareholders Friday that Stratosphere's performance would no longer have any material effect on Grand Casinos' results.
"Grand Casinos has written off its 42 percent investment in Stratosphere," Berman said. "We no longer realize any effect on our financial results of Stratosphere's operations."
Grand Casinos operating margins have been narrowing because expenses have grown faster than revenues.

But chief financial officer Timothy Cope told Reuters following the meeting that he expects the casino operating margins to stabilize or begin to widen in 1997 as expenses grow at the same rate as, or slower than, revenues.

"The relationship between the two should stay about flat, or casino expenses' relationship to casino revenues should go down slightly'" Cope said. "A lot of the increase in casino expenses was caused by marketing programs we put in place in 1996, and now we've pared it back. Also, as the casino revenues grow at Tunica without any additional expenses, that should change the relationship."
Casino operating margin narrowed to 65 percent in 1996 from 70 percent in 1995. Expenses grew 54 percent to $126.1 million while revenues grew 34 percent to $361.8 million, the company said.
Berman told Reuters the company's hotel revenues would continue to assume a larger share of gross revenues, but that hotel operating margins probably would not continue to widen.

"We are committed to opening more rooms, so hotel revenues will become a bigger percentage of our base," Berman said. "We think its a very good return on investment, but margins will probably remain about the same."

Hotel revenues increased to 4.8 percent of gross revenues in 1996, from 2.8 percent in 1995. Hotel operating margin increased to 75 percent in 1996, from 67 percent in 1995. Grand Casinos shares were off 1/8 at 13-3/4 Monday.
